interactions.prompt: how do i start adapting the unet model we made in lab 3 for our elec5308 project? i want to train it using the webots images and segmentation data and have 7 classes for the ground truth
interactions.response: You can adapt the Lab 3 U-Net by keeping the same general encoder-decoder structure but changing the final output layer to produce 7 classes. The Webots RGB camera images can be used as the input images, while the corresponding Webots segmentation information can be processed into 7-class ground truth masks. The training pipeline can then use each RGB image together with its matching mask to train the model. After training, the best model weights can be saved and loaded later by the Webots controller for inference.

metaReflection.processEvolution: At first i was asking how to adapt the lab 3 code in general. Then i started giving more details about our webots setup and the 7 classes we needed. After that i asked more specific questions about the training code, the ground truth masks and how everything would connect to the final webots controller.
metaReflection.criticalMoment: I had to check the actual data coming from webots because the class mapping was not something i could just assume. I used what i knew about the webots simulation and the output masks to check the pixel values and make sure the mapping to our 7 classes was actually correct.
metaReflection.skillDependency: The hardest part without AI would have been understanding how to take the lab 3 U-Net and change it into something that worked with our webots dataset. In particular, setting up the masks, class mapping, tensor dimensions and training pipeline would have taken much longer to work out.
metaReflection.synthesis: I learned how the U-Net training pipeline connects the camera images to the ground truth masks and how the model produces one class for each pixel. The AI helped me understand the structure and gave me ideas for the implementation, but i learned that i still need to check the actual webots data and test the code because some of the assumptions made by AI were not always exactly right.
